head: iPhone alarm volume too low? iOS 27 has a separate alarm slider
dek: iOS 27 lets your iPhone alarm ring at its own volume, separate from your ringtone, so a quiet ringer no longer means a quiet alarm. The setting is off by default, so alarms still follow the ringtone volume until you change it.
details: In Settings, Sounds & Haptics now has two sections: Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds. Each has a Match Ringtone Volume switch that's on by default. Turn it off under Alarms and Timers and a slider appears that sets only the volume of alarms and timers, so you can put alarms at full volume while calls and notifications stay quiet.
where: iPhone with iOS 27, in Settings now
means: If you've slept through an alarm because your ringer was turned down, you can now keep the alarm loud without making every call and notification just as loud.
todo: Open Settings, then Sounds & Haptics. Under Alarms and Timers, turn off Match Ringtone Volume and move the new slider to the level you want.
thumb_words: IPHONE ALARM GETS ITS OWN VOLUME
